subject: Private offer + capacity staircase: CloudForge renewal and ramp
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@cloudforge.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudForge Procurement <procure@cloudforge.com>
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning + capacity uplift (AWS private offer)

Hi Rishi —

Thanks again for the kickoff last week. We were internalizing the usage trends and want to start the private offer paperwork for our upcoming renewal. High-level asks from procurement and engineering:

- Move from a 12-month term to 24 months (preference from finance for longer term).
- Staircase capacity increase: +50% committed units starting month 7 (we expect a steady ramp tied to feature launch).
- Single PO preferred from procurement, but finance will confirm final billing cadence.

I've attached a short spreadsheet with our projected monthly usage and a first-pass list of security docs we may need. Can you:

1) Confirm whether the marketplace private-offer flow supports a staircase commit (we prefer AWS private offers but are open to Azure if there are limitations).
2) Share a draft private-offer term sheet (pricing + acceptance window) so our legal can triage.

Procurement lead is cc'd here (procure@cloudforge.com) and legal will loop in Ethan Brooks (cc'd on follow-ups). We aim to have an internal sign-off by end of May so we can hit the June launch.

Thanks — looking forward to the draft.

Samantha Lee
Head of Platform Partnerships
CloudForge Inc

Attachments: CloudForge_Renewal_requirement.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@cloudforge.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + capacity uplift (AWS private offer)

Hi Samantha —

Appreciate the clear brief and the workbook — that's super helpful. Short answers up front:

- Yes, AWS private offers can represent staged/staircase commitments; we can reflect a +50% step starting month 7 in the PO. We will also outline fallback options (burst vs committed) if actual usage deviates.
- We'll prepare a v1 private-offer term sheet for you and a separate pricing appendix for the staircase schedule.

Next steps on our side:
- I'll loop in Priyom to assemble the pricing appendix and acceptance window options.
- Naomi will run the compliance checklist and confirm whether additional SOC2 evidence is needed for the expanded capacity.

Questions for you:
- Do you expect the PO to be a single lump-sum or split into fiscal tranches? Procurement's email suggested single PO but finance sometimes prefers tranches.
- Any hard constraints on the acceptance window (e.g., must sign by June 10 to hit internal procurement cutoff)?

Attaching a quick sketch of items we'll include in the private-offer PDF.

Cheers,
Rishi
Director, Cloud Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: initial-scope-notes.pdf (1 page summary)

From: CloudForge Procurement <procure@cloudforge.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Samantha Lee <samantha@cloudforge.com>
Date: Sat, 12 May 2028 08:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + capacity uplift (PO preference)

Hi Rishi / Samantha —

Procurement here. Quick clarification: CloudForge will issue a single PO for the full 24-month commitment. Finance would prefer an invoice schedule that supports monthly reconciliation, but the PO itself should cover the whole commitment (easier for our SAP flows).

Please include the following in the private-offer package:
- Line showing staircase committed units and effective month.
- Explicit acceptance window (we prefer 30 days).
- Billing terms: Net 45.
- Any credits or migration allowances in the first 30 days for testing.

We'll expect a DocuSign link once Redwood has a v2 private-offer ready. Attaching our standard PO template for reference.

Thanks,
CloudForge Procurement

Attachments: PO_template.docx (procurement template)

From: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: CloudForge Procurement <procure@cloudforge.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha@cloudforge.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Draft private-offer + pricing appendix (CloudForge)

Hi Samantha / Procurement team —

Thanks for the guidance. Attached is Redwood's v2 private-offer PDF and a short pricing appendix that models the staircase:

- Term: 24 months
- Base committed units: 1.0x (months 1–6)
- Staircase: 1.5x from month 7 onwards (per your ask)
- Billing: Invoiced monthly, PO covers full commitment; Net 45 payment terms
- Acceptance window: 30 days (we can extend to 45 if your legal needs more time)
- Canary activation: optional 2-week canary at 10% traffic before full ramp

Pricing summary (monthly committed cost):
- Months 1–6: $45,000 / month (committed)
- Months 7–24: $67,500 / month (committed, reflects 1.5x)

Links: HubSpot opportunity (internal) and a draft DocuSign envelope are below for tracking and signature review.

Please confirm:
1) Acceptance window (30 vs 45 days).
2) Whether procurement still wants single PO (we've modeled that).
3) If you want the canary activated prior to month 7.

We will update the DocuSign envelope once you confirm the acceptance window and invoicing cadence.

Thanks — looking forward to final signoff.

— Priyom Das
Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_PrivateOffer_CLOUDFORGE_v2.pdf
Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/CF-2028-08-27, https://www.docusign.net/recipient/accept?pk=abc123-privateoffer-cloudforge

From: Samantha Lee <samantha@cloudforge.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>, CloudForge Procurement <procure@cloudforge.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Ethan Brooks <ebrooks@cloudforge.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft private-offer + pricing appendix (CloudForge)

Priyom / team —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and clear modeling. A few quick confirmations from CloudForge:

- Acceptance window: we'll take 45 days to give our legal time to review the appendix and the staircase language. Ethan (cc) will drive the redlines if any.
- PO: Procurement confirms single PO that covers the full 24 months; invoices should still be monthly for reconciliation.
- Canary: yes, we'd like the 2-week canary at ~10% traffic in week 2 of month 6 (so we can validate the ramp before month 7).
- Minor ask: can Redwood include a 30‑day service credit window if there is a failed canary activation? That protects our launch window.

If you can update the DocuSign envelope with acceptance window = 45 days and the canary credit language, we'll route for signature and aim to return the signed PO within two weeks.

Thanks — Samantha
Head of Platform Partnerships
CloudForge Inc
